# Spar 0.6.1

**A challenge you already did and the challenge you are on were two different
screens. 0.6.1 makes them one, so stepping back through a session is travel
rather than the app rebuilding itself — and cleans up the type, the sidebar and
the Problems page on the way.**

## Stepping through a session

- **One layout for a live challenge and a past one.** The workspace set the
  title at 17px over a 40px emblem and went straight into the problem; the
  standalone page set it under a "CHALLENGE 4" eyebrow over a 64px emblem and
  reached the problem four labelled sections later. Both now draw from the same
  component, so the two views are identical from the top of the page down to the
  end of the statement.
- **The crossing is a fade, not a teardown.** The two surfaces stay mounted
  together and cross-fade. Editors, drafts and scroll positions survive, so
  stepping back is instant instead of another cold load.
- **No more "Opening challenge…" on the way in.** The challenge is read before
  the page opens rather than after, so the first frame is the problem.
- **The brief keeps its width.** The two surfaces persisted two different panel
  splits, so the problem column changed width every time a step crossed between
  them. They now share one saved layout: drag the divider on either side and the
  other is already where you left it.
- **Back is up and forward is down.** The stepper reads as the column it is —
  the ordinal rolls in the direction you travelled, and the body moves with it.

## Fixed

- **The live challenge's editor could go blank.** With both surfaces mounted,
  the practice page and the workspace shared one Monaco model, and the practice
  page disposed it as soon as it read its first file. Practice files are
  namespaced now.
- **Grid tiles sliced their own tags in half.** A wrapped tag row had nowhere to
  go in a fixed-height card and was cut through by the footer's rule. The row is
  a single line that cannot wrap, with the rest counted.

## Problems

- **The page leads with a pick.** The ranking was always in the order, but an
  ordered list with no top to it reads as an index. The first suggestion is now
  drawn as a recommendation, with the reason it is first.
- **Filters stay with you.** Search, source, level, status and sort are a sticky
  toolbar across the pane instead of a bar that scrolls away above eighty rows.
- **Rows are ruled and full-bleed**, with one pill each instead of four competing
  boxes, tags as text, and counts in lining figures so a column of them can be
  read down.
- **Spar signs its own work with its name.** The sparkle on a Spar-written
  problem was the app's icon for generated-by-a-model, which is what wrote it,
  not whose it is.

## Type and chrome

- **The interface is set in the platform's own face** — SF Pro on macOS, Segoe
  UI Variable on Windows — and antialiased. Only the wordmark uses Poppins.
- **Sidebar rows are 15px at a weight that holds on glass**, with solid icons.
  Alpha text composites against the desktop twice and arrives grey, so rank is
  carried by fill and colour rather than by thinning the ink.
- **Sessions wear their language's mark** in its own colour, rather than a
  procedurally generated shape that says nothing about the row beside it.
- **The toolbar dropped its grey session line.** The session is named in full
  where you would go looking for it.

## Downloads

| Your machine | File |
| --- | --- |
| Mac, Apple silicon | `Spar-0.6.1-arm64.dmg` |
| Mac, Intel | `Spar-0.6.1.dmg` |
| Windows | `Spar-0.6.1-x64.exe` |
| Linux | `Spar-0.6.1-x86_64.AppImage` or `Spar-0.6.1-amd64.deb` |

## Known limits

- This open distribution is unsigned. macOS Gatekeeper or Windows SmartScreen
  may ask you to approve the first launch, and those platforms may require a
  manual installer step for an update.
- Linux AppImage installations can self-update when the runtime supports it;
  `.deb` installations remain managed by the system package manager.
